feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: Oregon governor Tina Kotek reacts to Silver Rail Elementary school shooting
entry.summary: NPR's Joel Rose talks with Oregon Governor Tina Kotek about the shooting at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon.

entry.title: Student protests widen into greater social unrest in France
entry.summary: Hundreds of protests took place in cities across France. Most of them were peaceful but some turned chaotic and violent.

entry.title: Iowa's vote in midterms may help determine balance of power in Congress
entry.summary: Iowa Public Radio's Natalie Krebs reports on how Iowa - a state that reliably votes Republican for president - has some competitive races for Republicans in November, which could help determine the balance of power in Congress.

entry.title: President Trump's widening stamp on D.C. landmarks
entry.summary: NPR's Joel Rose and Rachel Treisman met at East Potomac Golf Links, a golf course that President Trump has ambitions to transform, to discuss the president's widening stamp on D.C. landmarks.

entry.title: The state of the State Department in the wake of the Kimberly Guilfoyle scandal
entry.summary: NPR's Joel Rose talks with James B. Story, former U.S. Ambassador to Venezuela, about the state of the State Department in the wake of the Kimberly Guilfoyle scandal.

entry.title: Biking along the Great American Rail-Trail
entry.summary: Organizers hope to connect more than 150 existing rail-trails, greenways and other paths spanning more than 3,700 miles across America. NPR's Joel Rose checks on their progress in western Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Ohio.

entry.title: How public bathrooms reflect America's inequality
entry.summary: Public restrooms are scarce in cities across the U.S. It's a topic historian and Temple University professor Bryant Simon writes about in his new book 'For Customers Only: Public Bathrooms and the Making of American Inequality.'

entry.title: Mayor of Bend shares how her community is doing after elementary school shooting
entry.summary: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Mayor of Bend Melanie Kebler about how the community is grieving the three children and teacher who were killed in a shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School on Thursday.

entry.title: Here's what experts say about the civilian intervention in the Bend school shooting
entry.summary: An armed bystander stopped a shooting at a school in Bend, Ore. We talk with experts about how rarely an armed civilian ends an attack like this and how gun rights groups are responding.

entry.title: 'Where is Austin Tice': NPR series investigates a journalist's disappearance in Syria
entry.summary: A new investigative series by NPR looks into the real life missing person case of American journalist Austin Tice, who disappeared in Syria over a decade ago.
